messages.subject: Re: shinyapps - shiny server : An ERROR HAS OCCURRED
messages.subject_clean: shinyapps - shiny server : An ERROR HAS OCCURRED
messages.body_plain:
The size of the directory does not necessarily correspond to the memory requirements of your application.
Have you tried using a larger instance size with more memory?

FWIW, each instance will have the same memory requirements, as each one would be loading your data set and performing computations.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Hosting shinyapp with very large datasets
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Hosting shinyapp with very large datasets
messages.body_plain:
Daniel,

The maximum application size supported by shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is 5GB, and the maximum amount of memory we allow is 8GB (on paid plans only). With such a large dataset, I don't think shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> will work very well for your use case. I would suggest looking into running shiny-server or shiny-server pro on your own server.

Hope that helps,
-Andy

It's not a memory problem (according to my dashboard, it maxes out below 50 MB), or a timeout problem. I would greatly appreciate any help debugging this.

TIA,
Paul

Sure. It's https://parubin.shinyapps.io/scm871/. You'll need a data set in a .xlsx file to test it. I've been using a couple of the data sets that come with R, including the Duncan employment data (4.8 KB Excel file). All the app does (when it works) is plot individual variables, let the user run a linear regression, and then provide some diagnostic plots and tests.

In the first tab, upper left in the left panel, there's a button to upload your data. There are controls to pin down where in the Excel file the data is, but if your data is in the first tab with nothing other than maybe empty cells above it, you should be able to skip them. Once the data has been inhaled, there's a tab with a DT showing the data. That does not seem to be a crash source. I can sort columns and such without a server disconnect.

The next tab lets you plot one variable, and optionally plot the interaction of two variables, and the tab after that lets you specify a linear model. When I do anything with either of those tabs, the server usually disconnects immediately. I've had a couple of instances where I could plot one variable okay, but whatever I did next triggered the disconnect. Other times, even plotting one variable blows it up.

Just to repeat, the same application code is running in a paid account with no problems, and the dev version was running fine until a day or so ago. The only thing I can think of that might have changed in the dev version was the versions of the supporting libraries.

Thanks for responding.

Paul

library(rgdal)

logo <- system.file("pictures/Rlogo.jpg", package="rgdal")[1]
x <- GDAL.open(logo)
opar <- par(no.readonly=TRUE)
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
displayDataset(x, band=1, reset.par=FALSE)
displayDataset(x, band=2, reset.par=FALSE)
displayDataset(x, band=3, reset.par=TRUE)
par(opar)
dx <- RGB2PCT(x, band=1:3)
displayDataset(dx)
GDAL.close(x)
GDAL.close(dx)

I am surprised that disabling the package cache didn't do the trick, but hopefully this is fixed now.

Hi I also have the problem with plots on shiny remote server. On my local device everything works fine, but on a remote device I can onlu see the ui checkbox.
Here is a link to the app:  https://mikolajm.shinyapps.io/MCA_test/
I would be very grateful for any the help.

And a reproducible code of the app:

library(shiny)
library(FactoMineR)
library(cluster)
data(tea)

ui <- fluidPage(

  titlePanel("MCA"),

  fluidRow(
        column(6, checkboxGroupInput("Variables", "Select variables:",
                                 names(tea), selected=c("breakfast", "tea.time"))),
      column(6, plotOutput("plot"))),
  fluidRow(
    column(12, plotOutput("dendro", height = "700px", width="1200px"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

  tea_selected <- reactive({
    tea[, input$Variables]
  })

  ##  mca
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    library(FactoMineR)
    par(mfrow=c(2,2))
    tea.mca <- MCA(tea_selected(), ncp=9)
  })

  ### dendro

  output$dendro <- renderPlot({
    library(FactoMineR)
    library(cluster)

    tea.mca <- MCA(tea_selected(), ncp=9)
    classif <- agnes(tea.mca$ind$coord,method="ward")
    plot(classif,main="Dendrogram",ask=F,which.plots=2)
  })
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject_clean: Shinyapp keeps crashing and I dont know why? :(
messages.body_plain:
Hi y'all,

Hopefully someone can help me with the following:
My shiny app keeps on crashing (grey screen with the "disconnected from server" notification) when opened.
Sometimes it works fine for a couple of minutes and other times it just crashes.
The manual suggests that "the problem may still lie within your code", but I cannot find the problem (see code below).
Maybe a more experienced Shiny user can help me along?

I want to thank you in advance.

UI
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
shinyUI(fluidPage(sliderInput(inputId = "num",
                            label = "Kies diameter (km)",
                            value = 30,
                            min = 10,
                            max = 50),
                leafletOutput("Circle"),
        submitButton(text = "Update", icon("refresh"))
        )
        )

Server
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(sp)
library(rgeos)
library(gdata)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(RgoogleMaps)
library(rgdal)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

Grafiek <- read_csv("dealers.csv")
installaties <- read_csv("installaties.csv")
shapedata <- readOGR(".", "Gemeentegrenzen_2017_zonder_water")
shapedata2 <- spTransform(shapedata, CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_def"))
shape_and_data <- merge(shapedata2,installaties, by.y = "Gemeentecode", by.x = "code")
pal <- colorNumeric(palette = "BuPu", domain = shape_and_data$Aantal)
shinyServer(function(input, output, session){

  output$Circle <- renderLeaflet(
    {
      leaflet()%>%
        addTiles()%>%
        addMarkers(data = Grafiek,
                   lng =  Grafiek$longitude,
                   lat =  Grafiek$latitude,
                   popup = Grafiek$ID)%>%
        addLegend("bottomright",
                  pal = pal,
                  values = shape_and_data$Aantal,
                  title = "Legenda",
                  opacity = 1)
    }
  )

  observe(
    leafletProxy("Circle")%>%
      clearShapes%>%
      addPolygons(data = shape_and_data,
                  fillColor = ~pal(shape_and_data$Aantal),
                  fillOpacity = 0.75,
                  color = "#000",
                  weight = 1,
                  group = shape_and_data$gemeentena)%>%
      addCircles(data = Grafiek,
                 lng =  Grafiek$longitude,
                 lat =  Grafiek$latitude,
                 group = Grafiek$ID,
                 radius = input$num*1000,
                 color = "#FF3333",
                 weight = 0.5)

  )

})

If you have a starter plan, you will not be billed for overages. After 100 hours your account will be suspended, preventing your applications from loading. -Andy

messages.subject: Re: Google sheets authentication in Shin apps
messages.subject_clean: Google sheets authentication in Shin apps
messages.body_plain:
With Flexdashboard documents / Rmarkdown docs you can specify the resource_files required within the same directory as the application file.

Example:

---
title: "My Flexdashboard"
resource_files:
- .httr-oauth
---

You may be able to something similar with the function addResourcePath and specify the file that way.

https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/addResourcePath.html

messages.subject: I am developing shiny apps for work and I need to know if, when anyone uses the app, the loaded data is stored or deleted when the user stops the app.
messages.subject_clean: I am developing shiny apps for work and I need to know if, when anyone uses the app, the loaded data is stored or deleted when the user stops the app.
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I think I know the answer but I would like to hear it in a less "bureaucratic" language.

I believe, from reading this post (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40879254/r-shiny-is-uploaded-data-safe-and-secure), that the safety and policies concerning data depend on the server you use and that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is a safe option and fits my needs in terms of not making one's data public in any way.

So..

When a user/colleague uses the Shiny App through Shinyapps.io and uploads data on it, will that data be public? Will the data be deleted right after the end of the user's session? Is the Stackoverflow post saying what I think it's saying?

Thank you very much,

CP

messages.body_plain:
Yes, you would use odbcDriverConnect and supply a connection string.

shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> has the unixodbc system package installed, with MySQL, PostgreSQL and FreeTDS drivers configured.

Consult your database's documentation for an appropriate IP/hostname based connection string, but here are a couple examples I had lying around:

odbcDriverConnect(connection = "Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=7.2;Server=mydns.database.windows.net <http://mydns.database.windows.net>;Port=1433;Database=mydatabase;Uid=myuserid;Pwd=mypass;Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;Connection Timeout=30;")
odbcDriverConnect('driver=MySQL;server=xxxx;database=dbname;uid=username;pwd=password;')
